title: File Box Story Turning Point Card Pack
audience: Families, homeschool groups, tutors, and adult-led writing tables for writers ages 7-11.
sessionLength: 16 printable file box story turning-point cards plus adult guide tools, turning-point routines, take-home turning slips, and optional adult prompts
safetyNote: No scary harm, no bullying, no romance, no weapons, no branded characters, and no identifying facts.

cover.kicker: Printable file box turning point cards
cover.headline: File Box Story Turning Point Card Pack
cover.subhead: Sixteen file-box cards help writers connect a starting scene, a turn signal, a before path, an after path, a character reaction, and a next step.
included: 16 printable file box turning point cards

adultGuide.title: File Box Turning Point Adult Guide
bullets: Adult-led setup: place the file box, blank pages, pencils, and one turning point card on the table before the writer begins: ____________________.
Adult-led framing: choose one fictional starting scene and keep every page paper-only, offline, and invented: ____________________.
Adult-led order: move from starting scene to turn signal, before path, after path, reaction, next step, and file-box label: ____________________.
Adult-led support: let the writer write or dictate short fictional lines while the adult keeps the file box sorted: ____________________.
Adult-led safety: use pretend characters, broad places, and invented actions instead of real names, exact places, or personal facts: ____________________.
Adult-led close: reread the turning point, add the next-step note, and write one file-box label for the paper stack: ____________________.

turningPointRoutines.title: Starting Scene File Card
turningPointRoutines.materials: File box, blank page, pencil, and starting scene card.
steps: The adult opens the file box and points to the starting scene blank: ____________________.
The writer names one fictional place where the page begins: ____________________.
The adult asks what the character is doing before anything changes: ____________________.
The writer writes or dictates one starting scene line on paper: ____________________.
turningPointRoutines.adultWrapLine: This paper turning point starts in this fictional scene: ____________________.

turningPointRoutines.title: Turn Signal Slip
turningPointRoutines.materials: File box, starting scene page, turn signal slip, and pencil.
steps: The adult rereads the starting scene line from the paper page: ____________________.
The writer invents one turn signal that shows the story is about to change: ____________________.
The adult asks what the character notices when the turn signal appears: ____________________.
The writer writes the turn signal on the slip and places it beside the page: ____________________.
turningPointRoutines.adultWrapLine: The turn signal changes the paper plan with: ____________________.

turningPointRoutines.title: Before Path Sort
turningPointRoutines.materials: File box, starting scene page, before path note, and pencil.
steps: The adult points to what the character expected before the turn signal: ____________________.
The writer names the before path the character thought would happen: ____________________.
The adult asks which paper line belongs before the turning point: ____________________.
The writer writes the before path note and files it behind the starting scene: ____________________.
turningPointRoutines.adultWrapLine: The before path on this paper plan is: ____________________.

turningPointRoutines.title: After Path Sort
turningPointRoutines.materials: File box, turn signal slip, after path note, and pencil.
steps: The adult slides the turn signal slip between the before path and the blank after path: ____________________.
The writer invents what changes after the turn signal: ____________________.
The adult asks how the after path is different from the before path: ____________________.
The writer writes the after path note and places it after the turn signal: ____________________.
turningPointRoutines.adultWrapLine: The after path changes the fictional page by: ____________________.

turningPointRoutines.title: Character Reaction Note
turningPointRoutines.materials: File box, before path note, after path note, reaction note, and pencil.
steps: The adult lays the before path and after path notes side by side: ____________________.
The writer names how the fictional character reacts to the change: ____________________.
The adult asks what the reaction shows in one paper line: ____________________.
The writer writes the character reaction note and tucks it after the after path: ____________________.
turningPointRoutines.adultWrapLine: The character reaction after the turning point is: ____________________.

turningPointRoutines.title: Next-Step File-Box Close
turningPointRoutines.materials: File box, page stack, next-step slip, file-box label strip, and pencil.
steps: The adult rereads the starting scene, turn signal, before path, after path, and reaction: ____________________.
The writer chooses one fictional next step that follows the turning point: ____________________.
The adult asks what file-box label will help find this paper turning point later: ____________________.
The writer writes the next-step slip and file-box label, then the adult files the stack: ____________________.
turningPointRoutines.adultWrapLine: The file-box label closes this turning point as: ____________________.
